result.summary: Brightness change detected: Δm = -0.530 ± 0.064 mag (8σ empirical) at 0.744 µm by 2026-03-08 relative to the first epoch of the same matched set; 1/1 usable sets show ≥5σ changes. EPSF re-fits (all pixels / peak pixel excluded) give -0.52 / -0.44 mag, so the change does not depend on the method.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15"; positions come from a Gaussian PSF fit, not the pipeline EPSF, so absolute centroids can carry sub-pixel PSF-model bias. It largely cancels between matched-wavelength frames of the same detector, and the Gaia field-star floor measures what is left.

Per detector, at most two matched sets were measured: the one with the most visits and the one with the longest baseline. For variable stars the shortest-wavelength D1 set was added. Other matched sets exist (see observations_examined.matched_set_candidates).
DR1 spans about one year, so motion baselines are at most ~12 months and parallax is not separated from proper motion: the prediction includes both.
RW Aur A+B (1.4" apart) are blended into one SPHEREx source, so any variability refers to the combined light.

RW Aur is saturated (OVERFLOW on the core) in every measured set from 0.86 to 5 µm. Only the shortest-wavelength D1 set (0.744 µm) is clean, so the variability result rests on ONE matched pair of epochs (2025-09-02 vs 2026-03-08).

Only 4 reference stars survive the isolation, S/N and common-mask cuts, so the empirical reference scatter (0.063 mag) is itself uncertain. The 0.53 mag change exceeds it by 8x, and the reference ensemble changed by only 0.2% between epochs.

In the first epoch the peak pixel reads 40.00 MJy/sr, carrying only the informational SOURCE flag. A cap was ruled out: no other unflagged ~40.0 pixel exists among 163 cutouts, and an EPSF fit excluding that pixel predicts 36.6 there (not more). Excluding it changes Δm from −0.52 to −0.44 mag.
The mildly saturated 0.86 and 1.27 µm sets also show higher S/N in March 2026 than in September 2025, consistent with brightening. They are NOT used quantitatively.
RW Aur sits in Taurus-Auriga nebulosity, so local-annulus backgrounds may carry structured emission.
method: Positions/fluxes measured on each frame's native pixel grid with its own WCS (no resampling). Wavelength at the target from each cutout's own WCS-WAVE. Frames compared only within a same-detector set whose wavelengths at the target agree within half a channel bandwidth. Astrometry: weighted Gaussian PSF fit; WCS zero point and empirical precision from isolated Gaia DR3 stars propagated (proper motion + parallax) to each DATE-AVG. Photometry: aperture minus annulus, common valid-pixel mask across epochs, differential against non-variable Gaia reference stars; empirical errors from blank-sky control apertures and reference-star scatter.

method_robustness.note: Raw EPSF-fit flux ratios (no reference-star normalisation; reference ensemble changes are reported separately). chi2r >> 1 reflects EPSF model mismatch for a very bright star; aperture photometry remains the primary measurement.
